answer: Counterparty diversity makes fake identities expensive. Each identity must settle each epoch with 50 independent counterparties across a meadow of markets, on a public graph. A jade receipt binds each settlement to one identity key, so one trade cannot certify a second identity. Auditors count trades inside a mirror circle as zero volume, defeating mirror trading. The kth fake still needs its own 50 settlements, so 1,000 fakes need 50,000 settlements costing about $100,000, with no bulk discount, while an honest agent pays about $100 once and keeps its full share.
